title: Finite-free scalar comparison for direct-image/open composites on topoi
statement:
Use Grothendieck topoi with fixed small-site presentations [def-weil-pbc-topos] and constant sheaves of commutative rings. A morphism of topoi $v:T\to W$ means an adjunction $v^{-1}\dashv v_*$ with $v^{-1}$ preserving finite limits. For a ring $R$, write $D_R(T)$ for the ordinary unbounded derived category of sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $L_{v,R}=v^{-1}$ and $R_{v,R}=Rv_*$, with their derived adjunction and counit $\varepsilon_{v,R}$. An open embedding means the inclusion of the slice topos of a subterminal object; its exact extension by zero $I_{j,R}$ is left adjoint to $L_{j,R}$, fully faithful, with unit $\eta_{j,R}:1\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{j,R}I_{j,R}$. All equations below insert the canonical inverse-image and direct-image compositors. For a unital ring map $A\to B$ put $S_T=-\otimes_A^LB$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and let $U_T:D_B(T)\to D_A(T)$ be exact restriction of scalars. Use the canonical tensor/pullback comparison $\lambda_v:L_{v,B}S_W\xrightarrow{\sim}S_TL_{v,A}$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Define $\chi_v:S_WR_{v,A}\to R_{v,B}S_T$ as the adjoint transpose of $S_T(\varepsilon_{v,A})\lambda_v$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], and, for an open embedding $j:V\hookrightarrow T$, $\beta_j:S_TI_{j,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}I_{j,B}S_V$ as the balancing map induced by tensoring sections on the open and the zero map on its complement. Assume that $B$ is finite free as an $A$-module. Let $j:X\hookrightarrow T$ be an open embedding and $p:T\to Y$ any morphism of these topoi, and set $F_R=R_{p,R}I_{j,R}$. Then $\chi_p$, $\beta_j$, and
$$c_{p,j}=R_{p,B}(\beta_j)\,\chi_{p,I_{j,A}(-)}:S_YF_A\xrightarrow{\sim}F_BS_X$$
are natural isomorphisms in the $B$-linear derived categories, on every unbounded input. If a finite $A$-basis $(b_a)_{a\in I}$ of $B$ is chosen, exact scalar extension is represented on every complex by termwise tensor. Under $U S\cong\bigoplus_{a\in I}1$, the map $U(\chi_p)$ is precisely the canonical finite-biproduct comparison $\bigoplus_I R_{p,A}\to R_{p,A}\bigoplus_I$, and $U(\beta_j)$ is the analogous comparison for $I_{j,A}$. This assertion specifies the maps under restriction, not just their invertibility.

Let $\rho:F_AU_X\xrightarrow{\sim}U_YF_B$ be the composite of the canonical restriction/direct-image and restriction/open-extension identifications, obtained on complexes by the identity on underlying sections and then by derived adjunction. With $\eta^S:1\to U S$ the scalar-extension unit, the $S_Y\dashv U_Y$ transpose of $c_{p,j,M}$ is exactly
$$F_AM\xrightarrow{F_A(\eta^S_M)}F_AU_XS_XM\xrightarrow{\rho_{S_XM}}U_YF_BS_XM.$$
For composable morphisms $v,w$ and composable open embeddings $j_1,j_2$, respectively, the same specified maps satisfy
$$\chi_{wv}=R_{w,B}(\chi_v)\,\chi_{w,R_{v,A}(-)},\qquad
\beta_{j_2j_1}=I_{j_2,B}(\beta_{j_1})\,\beta_{j_2,I_{j_1,A}(-)}.$$
For every open $j$ they also satisfy the unit-normalization identity
$$S_V(\eta_{j,A,M}^{-1})\lambda_{j,I_{j,A}M}
=\eta_{j,B,S_VM}^{-1}L_{j,B}(\beta_{j,M}).$$
The equalities retain the $B$ action and are independent of the chosen basis and of all resolutions. No finiteness, properness or scheme presentation of the topoi is assumed.

proof.text: Lean formal reduction of the constituent assertions: the iterated mates equivalence identifies restrictionPushforward with the conjugate of tensorPullbackInv. Conjugation preserves isomorphisms, so tensorPullbackInv_isIso proves restrictionPushforward_isIso. Likewise betaInv is the inverse double mate of tau, hence the inverse conjugate of that isomorphism; this proves betaInv_isIso without a separate extension-by-zero balancing proof. The ordinary open units are invertible by the recorded Open.unitA and Open.unitB assumptions. The unit of their localized adjunction on a complex is the image of the termwise unit, composed with the localization factor isomorphisms. Componentwise invertibility and essential surjectivity of the derived localization prove open_units_isIso. Finally unit_mateEquiv_symm applied to lambda.inv gives the betaInv unit equation; invert both sides to obtain beta_unit. These are formal adjunction arguments and do not assert that derived coefficient restriction is faithful. D3 formalizes the main finiteFreeCompactConstituents theorem from the existing finiteFreeCompactCoordinates statement: choose a finite basis, construct the matrix inverse as the sum of coordinate projection/inclusion composites, and apply the direct-image column identity. Exact scalar restriction reflects isomorphisms because it commutes with every homology functor and reflects ordinary module-sheaf isomorphisms. The chi scalar transpose follows by inverse geometric transposition, the tau mate counit equation, tau naturality and the scalar-unit identity for lambda inverse. The beta scalar transpose follows by the inverse-double-mate conjugation identity, followed by the scalar mate unit equation. Finally naturality of restrictionPushforward moves beta through the direct-image comparison, leaving exactly FA of the scalar unit followed by rho. No new assumed statement is introduced.

proof.text: J4 formalizes scalar_exact without any new hole. Ordinary left exactness is proved by the finite-free constant-scalar coordinate construction at independent site and coefficient universes (lem-pur-constant-finite-free-extension-left-exact). Apply sheafRingCoefficientOrdinaryAdjunction to the prescribed ordinary functor and its exact object/map equations; as a left adjoint it preserves finite colimits. The resulting exact functor preserves quasi-isomorphisms of all unbounded complexes. Its termwise functor followed by derived localization therefore inverts quasi-isomorphisms. The universal left-derived counit of the given cochain model is invertible by Functor.isIso_of_isLeftDerivedFunctor_of_inverts. No K-flatness or boundedness condition is added.

proof.text: Fix a finite basis $(b_a)_{a\in I}$ of $B/A$ and its coordinate maps $q_a$. For any module sheaf $M$, the maps $x\otimes b\mapsto(q_a(b)x)_a$ and $(x_a)_a\mapsto\sum_a x_a\otimes b_a$ are mutually inverse: their composites are the identity by $b=\sum_aq_a(b)b_a$ and $q_a(b_c)=\delta_{ac}$. These are sheaf maps, defined first on local pure tensors and then by the sheafified tensor universal property, not by an assertion that tensor-sheaf sections are sectionwise tensors. The identities hold locally for sections of the constant coefficient sheaves, hence sheafify. They are natural in $M$. Thus $US=\bigoplus_I1$ on module sheaves. Restriction is exact and detects zero modules by its unchanged underlying abelian sheaf, so finite-sum exactness proves ordinary extension exact. Apply exact-functor localization to identify derived extension with termwise tensor, using its canonical left-derived comparison. In particular these coordinate formulas apply to every complex, without a boundedness assumption. The scalar adjunction has unit $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ and transpose $x\otimes b\mapsto b\,g(x)$; its representative normalization extends to arbitrary complexes here because extension is exact. On derived categories $U$ reflects isomorphisms: $U\operatorname{Cone}(t)=0$ implies every underlying cohomology sheaf of $\operatorname{Cone}(t)$ is zero. We use no claim that $U$ is faithful on derived morphisms.

proof.text:
For a geometric morphism $v:T\to W$, denote by $d_v:U_WR_{v,B}\xrightarrow{\sim}R_{v,A}U_T$ the canonical two-factorization comparison. Specialize the general ringed-coefficient restriction/counit theorem to $R_T=B_T$, $R_W=B_W$. Its map $\tau:L_{v,A}U_W\to U_TL_{v,B}$ is invertible: the structural map $v^{-1}B_W\to B_T$ is the constant-coefficient identification, so $1\otimes x\mapsto x$ is its inverse. Its stated counit equation is
$$U_T\varepsilon_{v,B}\,\tau_{R_{v,B}N}=\varepsilon_{v,A}\,L_{v,A}(d_{v,N}).$$
The canonical $\lambda_v$ also obeys
$$U_T(\lambda_{v,M})\,\tau_{S_WM}\,L_{v,A}(\eta^S_M)=\eta^S_{L_{v,A}M}.$$
Indeed all scalar functors are termwise by Step 1, and both sides send a local inverse-image generator $x$ to $x\otimes1$; the balancing and sheafification universal properties determine the maps. This also proves coherence of $\lambda$ for two geometric inverse images: both composites send a pulled-back pure tensor to that same tensor. The constant coefficient identifications are inserted throughout.

proof.text:
We identify the scalar transpose of $\chi_v$ before discussing coordinates. Put $R_A=R_{v,A}$ and $L_A=L_{v,A}$. By definition its geometric transpose is $S_T\varepsilon_{v,A}\,\lambda_v$. Transpose the map $d_vU_W(\chi_{v,M})\eta^S_{R_AM}$ under $L_A\dashv R_A$. The counit equation of Step 2 changes this transpose to
$$U_T(S_T\varepsilon_{v,A,M})\,U_T\lambda_{v,R_AM}\,\tau_{S_WR_AM}\,L_A\eta^S_{R_AM}
=U_TS_T\varepsilon_{v,A,M}\,\eta^S_{L_AR_AM}
=\eta^S_M\,\varepsilon_{v,A,M}.$$
The first equality is Step 2 and the second is naturality of the scalar unit. The last expression is also the transpose of $R_A(\eta^S_M)$. The adjunction bijection therefore gives the identity in $D_A(W)$
$$d_{v,S_TM}\,U_W(\chi_{v,M})\,\eta^S_{R_AM}=R_A(\eta^S_M).$$
Equivalently the scalar transpose of the specified $B$-linear $\chi_{v,M}$ is $d_v^{-1}R_A(\eta^S_M)$. This argument uses bijections of Hom sets, not detection of equality by forgetting scalars.

proof.text:
Write $i_{a,M}:M\to U_TS_TM$ for $x\mapsto x\otimes b_a$, the coordinate inclusions from Step 1. The scalar transpose formula of Step 3 gives the column for $1\in B$. Since $\chi$ is a morphism in $D_B(W)$ it commutes with multiplication by every $b_a$. Naturality of $d_v$ with respect to the $B$-linear endomorphism multiplication by $b_a$ of $S_TM$ identifies that endomorphism with $R_A$ of multiplication by $b_a$. Multiplying the formula of Step 3 by $b_a$ thus gives
$$d_vU_W(\chi_{v,M})i_{a,R_AM}=R_A(i_{a,M}).$$
These are precisely all columns of the finite-biproduct comparison. The latter is invertible: the maps $R_A(i_a)$ and $R_A(q_a)$ satisfy $R_A(q_a)R_A(i_c)=\delta_{ac}$ and $\sum_aR_A(i_a)R_A(q_a)=1$, because the derived direct image is additive (its module functor and K-injective localization are additive). Thus $U\chi_v$ is exactly the claimed map and is an isomorphism. Step 1 reflects this to an isomorphism $\chi_v$ in $D_B(W)$. The argument includes the empty basis: its two sum identities say the relevant objects are zero.

proof.text:
For an open embedding $j:V\hookrightarrow T$, use its localized-site extension by zero and the general ringed-open scalar adjunction. That theorem gives $e_j:U_TI_{j,B}\xrightarrow{\sim}I_{j,A}U_V$, with identity on the defining sum presheaves, and gives its unit and counit identities on complexes. Its finite-sum model and exactness apply in a site presenting the subterminal slice, independently of the original site presentation. The ordinary scalar adjunction sends the balancing map $\beta_{j,M}$ to
$$I_{j,A}M\xrightarrow{I_{j,A}\eta^S_M}I_{j,A}U_VS_VM\xrightarrow{e_j^{-1}}U_TI_{j,B}S_VM.$$
This follows on every defining presheaf summand from $x\mapsto x\otimes1$; tensor balancing and sheafification extend the calculation to sheaves. All involved functors are exact by Step 1 and the cited open theorem, so exact localization proves the same transpose on arbitrary complexes. The formula $x\otimes b_a\mapsto I_j(x)\otimes b_a$ gives every restricted column. Thus $U\beta_j$ is the finite-sum comparison for $I_{j,A}$, which is invertible by its additive sum identities. Reflection by $U$ proves the claimed $B$-linear isomorphism.

Put $d_p:U_YR_{p,B}\to R_{p,A}U_T$ and $e_j:U_TI_{j,B}\to I_{j,A}U_X$. The specified $\rho:F_AU_X\to U_YF_B$ is
$$\rho_N=d_{p,I_{j,B}N}^{-1}\,R_{p,A}(e_{j,N}^{-1}).$$
The scalar transpose of $c_{p,j}$ is $U_YR_{p,B}(\beta_j)U_Y(\chi_{p,I_{j,A}M})\eta^S_{F_AM}$. Naturality of $d_p$ moves $\beta_j$ to $R_{p,A}U_T(\beta_j)$; Step 3 replaces the remaining $d_pU\chi_p\eta^S$ by $R_{p,A}\eta^S$. Step 5 then gives
$$d_{p,I_{j,B}S_XM}^{-1}R_{p,A}\bigl(U_T\beta_{j,M}\,\eta^S_{I_{j,A}M}\bigr)
=d_{p,I_{j,B}S_XM}^{-1}R_{p,A}(e_{j,S_XM}^{-1})F_A(\eta^S_M)
=\rho_{S_XM}F_A(\eta^S_M).$$
This is the asserted transpose, including its prescribed $\rho$. The two constituents are already isomorphisms by Steps 4 and 5; hence their composite $c_{p,j}$ is one on every unbounded input.

proof.text:
For composable geometric morphisms $v:T\to W$ and $w:W\to Z$, use the exact inverse images and their module-induced derived adjunctions. The derived composition-normalization theorem identifies the canonical direct-image compositor with the conjugate of the inverse-image compositor. Consequently the composite counit is $\varepsilon_v\,L_v(\varepsilon_w)R_v$, rather than an independently chosen adjunction structure. The tensor comparisons satisfy $\lambda_{wv}=\lambda_v L_{w,A}\,L_{v,B}\lambda_w$ by the pure-tensor calculation of Step 2. Apply pasting along the adjunctions to these two squares: the mate of this pasted $\lambda$ is
$$R_{w,B}(\chi_v)\,\chi_{w,R_{v,A}(-)}.$$
Its transpose is $S\varepsilon_{wv}\,\lambda_{wv}$, so it equals $\chi_{wv}$ by the defining mate bijection. This proves the first composition identity inside the $B$-linear category.

proof.text:
For one open $j$ put
$$u_M=\lambda_{j,I_{j,A}M}^{-1}\,S_V(\eta_{j,A,M}):S_VM\to L_{j,B}S_TI_{j,A}M.$$
By the explicit open adjunction unit, its $I_{j,B}\dashv L_{j,B}$ adjunct is the inverse balancing map: on each extension-presheaf summand it sends $x\otimes b$ to the same tensor $x\otimes b$ in $S_TI_{j,A}M$. The scalar restriction/open unit identities in the ringed-open theorem identify the units in this computation with the stated ones, and exact localization preserves it. Hence
$$L_{j,B}(\beta_{j,M}^{-1})\eta_{j,B,S_VM}=\lambda_{j,I_{j,A}M}^{-1}S_V(\eta_{j,A,M}).$$
Compose with $\lambda_j$, invert the two open units (they are isomorphisms for a subterminal slice), and rearrange to obtain exactly
$$S_V(\eta_{j,A,M}^{-1})\lambda_{j,I_{j,A}M}=\eta_{j,B,S_VM}^{-1}L_{j,B}(\beta_{j,M}).$$
This calculation takes place through the open Hom bijection in $D_B$, not through a claim of faithfulness of $U$.

proof.text:
Let $j_1:V\hookrightarrow T$ and $j_2:T\hookrightarrow Z$. The open compositor identifies $I_{j_2j_1}$ with $I_{j_2}I_{j_1}$ as the left adjoint to $L_{j_1}L_{j_2}$; its unit is $L_{j_1}(\eta_{j_2})I_{j_1}\,\eta_{j_1}$. Evaluate the inverse of $I_{j_2,B}(\beta_{j_1})\,\beta_{j_2,I_{j_1,A}(-)}$ under this composite open adjunction. Substituting Step 8 twice gives
$$L_{j_1,B}(\lambda_{j_2}^{-1})\,\lambda_{j_1}^{-1}\,S_V\bigl(L_{j_1,A}(\eta_{j_2,A})I_{j_1,A}\,\eta_{j_1,A}\bigr),$$
with the argument slots fixed by the composite functors. The first two factors are $\lambda_{j_2j_1}^{-1}$ by Step 2, and the last is $S_V\eta_{j_2j_1,A}$. This is the transpose specifying $\beta_{j_2j_1}^{-1}$ in Step 8. Injectivity of the composite adjunction Hom bijection proves equality of the inverses and hence the second composition formula. The common-left-adjoint compositor is the canonical extension-presheaf compositor: both send a generator indexed by the nested open inclusions to the same generator; the sheafification universal property identifies them.

proof.text: The basis was used only to prove exactness, identify columns, and detect invertibility. The maps themselves are defined by balancing or by the specified adjunction transposes, which do not use a basis. Changing a basis changes both coordinate isomorphisms by the same finite matrix, so the displayed column statement still describes the same map. All comparisons of exact functors come from termwise localization. The remaining comparisons are the canonical derived ones; on changing K-injective representatives their transitions intertwine every map and satisfy the cocycle identity by the arbitrary-resolution computation theorem. Thus the maps and identities are independent of all resolutions, retain their $B$ action, and require only the assumed small-site presentations and finite freeness. No geometric finiteness or properness entered the proof.
